title: Pilot on-ramp: model selection and prompt heuristics
content:
Context:
Customer: Argentus (mid-market fintech) running a pilot for automated transaction summarization, risk-flagging, and compliance-extraction. Workload characteristics: short-to-medium documents (transaction descriptions + memo fields), heavy tail of weird char encodings and foreign-language snippets, 95th percentile request size ~450 tokens, median 120 tokens.

Primary success criteria (customer-facing):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end < 350ms for hosted path; < 200ms for Dedicated low-latency plan.
- Accuracy: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on labeled compliance set; summaries rated >= 4.3/5 on human eval sample.
- Cost: keep inference cost < $0.45 per 1k tokens (hosted target for pilot).
- Reliability: zero data leakage and support for region-specific hosting (EU).

Constraints and non-goals:
- Must avoid sending raw identifiers to third-party endpoints; private deployment preferred for regulated lanes.
- No large-context (>2k tokens) workflows in this pilot.
- Not testing multimodal.

Candidate model families considered (rationale):
- Mistral-7B: strong on short-context instruction tasks, low cost, compact. Candidate for extractor/re-ranker.
- Llama-2-13B (quantized): solid baseline for summarization quality when quantized; known latency on A100 is moderate.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (8-bit): top-tier quality for abstractive summarization but heavy on cost/latency — consider as fallback/validation model.
- Redwood-13B-v0 (internal curated variant): balanced performance, good quantization behaviour in our runtime.

Quantization strategies explored:
- 8-bit (int8) via manufacturer kernels: good latency reduction (~1.6x) with minimal quality drop for summarization.
- 4-bit GPTQ profile (per-channel): aggressive size reduction, noticeable drop in hallucination rates when combined with prompt scaffolding but some drop in extractive F1.
- AWQ-lite (mixed FP16/4-bit): best throughput on RTX6000 in our tests, slightly better fidelity vs GPTQ for this workload.
- Per-layer mixed precision: keep attention and final layers at FP16, quantize feedforward to 4-bit — useful trade for Llama-2-13B.

Small experiment summary (benchmarked on 1x A100 80GB and 1x RTX6000 for cost proxy):
- Setup: synthetic workload of 10k requests sampled from customer corpus, deterministic prompts for extraction/summarization. Measured p50/p95 latency, throughput (reqs/sec), extraction F1, ROUGE-L, and tokens/sec.
- Redwood-13B-v0 (FP16, A100): p95 = 320ms, throughput = 18 r/s, ext-F1 = 0.89, ROUGE-L = 0.62, cost est = $0.38 / 1k tokens.
- Redwood-13B-v0 (AWQ-lite 4-bit, A100): p95 = 210ms, throughput = 28 r/s, ext-F1 = 0.86, ROUGE-L = 0.60, cost est = $0.21 / 1k tokens.
- Mistral-7B (4-bit GPTQ, RTX6000): p95 = 140ms, throughput = 44 r/s, ext-F1 = 0.82, ROUGE-L = 0.55, cost est = $0.12 / 1k tokens.
- Falcon-40B (int8, A100): p95 = 610ms, throughput = 9 r/s, ext-F1 = 0.91, ROUGE-L = 0.68, cost est = $0.95 / 1k tokens.

Interpretation and recommendations from experiments:
- Two-stage cascade gives the best cost/latency/quality mix: cheap extractor (Mistral-7B 4-bit) -> concise canonicalizer -> mid-tier summarizer (Redwood-13B AWQ-lite). Reserve Falcon-40B for nightly high-quality validation or on-demand escalations.
- For extraction tasks where structured precision is required (F1 target >= 0.88), Redwood-13B in AWQ-lite hits threshold on this corpus; Mistral falls short. So we propose extraction route: Mistral quick-pass -> Redwood canonicalizer -> Redwood final extract (if high uncertainty reroute to Falcon).
- Prefix caching on frequent transaction templates yielded ~20% fewer tokens generated and ~12% p95 latency improvement in a short trial. Implement TTL 6 hours for template cache keys.

Prompt & pipeline tuning notes (what worked):
- Prompt scaffolding: explicit answer schema + strict tokens-of-interest markers reduced extraction hallucinations by ~9 percentage points. Example: "Return JSON with keys [merchant, amount, date, flags]; if unknown, return null."
- Chain-of-thought suppression (remove instruction to "think step-by-step") improved deterministic extraction — we avoid CoT for structured outputs.
- Temperature scheduling: set temperature=0 for extractor and canonicalizer, 0.1 for summarizer to keep concise language with minor creativity.
- Reranking: use a light LM reranker (Mistral-7B int8) to score 3 candidate outputs from Redwood-13B; picked-best increased human-rated quality by +0.06 points while adding ~65ms p95. Optional in Dedicated plan.

Operational controls and rollout plan:
- Canary (week 0-1): 5% traffic routed to new cascade (Mistral->Redwood). Monitor p95 latency, extraction F1 on labeled samples (daily), and error spikes.
- Ramp (week 2-3): 25% -> 50% traffic if SLOs preserved; enable prefix caching globally.
- Full (week 4+): 100% for non-sensitive lanes; region-locked traffic to Private deployment for EU regulated customers.

Runbook (short):
- If p95 rises > 25% from baseline for two consecutive 10-min windows: enable fallback single-model route (Redwood-13B FP16) and alert SRE.
- If extraction F1 drops > 4 points on daily labeled sample: re-route all uncertain extractions to Falcon-40B batch job for verification; open ticket with SE team.
- Manual rollback: rollback flavor to Redwood-13B FP16 and disable caching.

Cost knobs for customer conversations:
- Increase use of Mistral for cheap prefiltering to shave ~40% of tokens hitting expensive models.
- Tighten prefix cache TTLs and increase cache hit targets from 18% -> 30%.
- Introduce asynchronous quality checks: do final high-cost Falcon runs at off-peak in batches instead of inline for a subset of records.

Open questions / risks:
- Does the customer accept the two-tiered hybrid hosted/private routing for regulated flows? Need compliance signoff.
- Long tail of foreign-language memos performed worse with base quantized models — do we add language-detection + per-language model routing?
- AWQ deployment maturity across all hardware we expect in Dedicated (NVIDIA vs AMD) — need infra validation.

Next steps (action items):
- (Priya) Draft customer one-pager with recommended cascade and cost/latency tradeoffs (due 2024-11-27).
- (Liam) Run targeted language-detection experiments and produce routing matrix (due 2024-12-05).
- (Avery) Infra validation for AWQ profiles on Dedicated GPU types (due 2024-12-12).
- (Noah) Add prompt scaffolds as versioned artifacts in Console and create test harness for A/B prompts (due 2024-12-08).

Notes-to-self and workshop artifacts:
- Slack thread: #se-argentus-pilot contains raw logs and sample failure cases (link pinned in Confluence).
- Example curious failure (copy-paste): input with concatenated IBAN + emoji => extractor returned merchant=null; canonicalizer normalized date incorrectly. Add normalization step for emoji noise.
- Keep experiment notebooks in repo: experiments/argentus/pilot_v1 (work-in-progress).

Summary (one-liner):
Recommend a cost-conscious two-stage cascade (Mistral prefilter + Redwood-13B AWQ summarizer/extractor) with Falcon-40B as validation/backstop; pair with prompt scaffolding, prefix caching, and controlled canary rollouts to meet latency, quality, and cost targets for the Argentus pilot.
